subject: Re: MAP DRAFT: Data handling & compliance (retention, logging, PHI constraints)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lila Thompson <lila@healthlytics.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 15:02:00 -0000
Subject: MAP DRAFT: Data handling & compliance (post-call)

Hi Lila — thanks again for the call today. As promised, attaching the initial Mutual Action Plan (MAP) milestone focused on data handling & compliance so your team can review and confirm responsibilities/timelines. High level recap from our discovery: you need hosted inference for clinical summarization with strict retention windows, audit logging for all API calls, and a PHI-handling exception policy (no storage of raw PHI beyond ephemeral inference).

Key asks I noted: 
- Confirm maximum retention window (default vs. extended for audit)
- Clarify whether token-level logging is acceptable if redaction occurs at ingest
- Provide the list of endpoints that will send PHI

Attached: MAP_Draft_v1 (milestone list). Please review the milestone owners and proposed target close date.

Next steps: 
1) Your review and any changes to responsibilities by Feb 13
2) Security questionnaire / SOC2 artifacts exchange (we can share SOC2 attestation)
3) Schedule 30m security call (Aditya + Dev + Healthlytics Sec)

Thanks — I updated the doc with our initial assumptions; if you prefer, I can convert to a timeline view.


Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwoodinference.com

From: Lila Thompson <lila@healthlytics.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: James Park <j.park@healthlytics.com>, Procurement <procurement@healthlytics.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0000
Subject: Re: MAP DRAFT: Data handling & compliance (post-call)

Thanks Marissa — quick clarifying Qs after skimming the MAP draft: 
1) For PHI, we cannot allow storage of raw PHI anywhere persistent. Can Redwood support an "ephemeral-only" token policy where raw input is never written to disk and only kept in-memory for inference?
2) For audit logging, we need immutable audit trails with a 7-year retention for security events related to clinical workflows. Can you folks commit to that retention for audit logs (or provide an export path to our log store)?
3) For redaction: we will likely do client-side redaction for PII before hitting the API for most flows, but there will be a small set of endpoints that send raw PHI (e.g., claim ingestion). We need assurance of access controls and key management (KMS/HSM).

Also tagging Procurement — we need the mutual action plan to show clear procurement milestones (PO, legal review, sign).

Lila
Director of Product, Healthlytics

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lila Thompson <lila@healthlytics.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 18:45:00 -0000
Subject: Re: MAP DRAFT: Data handling & compliance (post-call)

Lila — great questions, thanks. I updated the MAP (attached v2) with explicit milestones and owners to reflect the PHI/retention/keys discussion. Summary of the changes and our proposed commitments: 

- Ephemeral-only inference: Redwood supports ephemerality for hosted/private deployments. We can enable an "ephemeral mode" flag per-route so raw inputs are kept in-memory only; no disk persistence and no long-term KV cache for those routes. Owner: Dev Patel (Redwood). Target: Feb 26, 2026.

- Audit logging & 7-year retention: We can stream immutable audit logs to your cloud log sink (S3/GCS) with signed delivery and 7-year lifecycle. Redwood retains request/response logs only if configured; default hosted retention is 30 days but we'll configure a dedicated export for Healthlytics. Owner: Aditya Rao (Redwood) + Healthlytics Sec. Target: Mar 5, 2026 (export pipeline live). Dependency: Healthlytics to provide destination bucket and IAM role.

- KMS/HSM & access controls: Support for customer-managed keys (Cloud KMS / HSM) is available for Private and Dedicated. For hosted we offer CMEK options and role-based access controls; we will include key rotation and audit hooks in the plan. Owner: Dev Patel (Redwood). Target: Mar 12, 2026.

- Procurement & legal milestones: PO submission (Healthlytics) by Feb 20; counter-sign and contract redlines complete by Mar 1. Owner: Healthlytics Procurement / Redwood Legal.

Attachments: Healthlytics_MAP_Draft_v2.pdf (MAP with milestone table), SOC2-Attestation.pdf (redwood attestation).

Next steps: 
- Can you confirm the audit log destination (bucket project + IAM) by Feb 18?
- Do you want Redwood to run a short architecture review with your security team next week (30m)?

If this looks good I will update HubSpot deal and convert MAP to a timeline milestone view.

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Lila Thompson <lila@healthlytics.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 11:30:00 -0000
Subject: Re: MAP DRAFT: Data handling & compliance (post-call)

Looping in a quick internal note for visibility (Lila, feel free to ignore). I scheduled the security architecture sync with Healthlytics Sec for Feb 19 14:00 PT — invite sent. Action items I picked up: 
- I will set up the log delivery template and a sample CloudFormation/IAM policy for the S3 destination. (Target: Feb 23)
- Dev — please confirm ephemeral-mode implementation details and whether the flag can be toggled per-route without redeploying models.
- Marissa — I'll update the HubSpot deal record (DL-2026-0142) with the MAP milestones and the expected close date Mar 15, 2026.

Thanks —
Aditya
